forest_mountain.name: Forest & Mountain Soils
forest_mountain.geological_origin: Formed in high-altitude forest ecosystems under varying precipitation; heavily influenced by aspect, slope, and snowline.
forest_mountain.texture: Loamy and silty in valley basins; coarse-grained, gravelly, and stony on steep upper ridges.
forest_mountain.chemical_profile: Rich in organic matter (humus) in dense forest tracts; acidic with low humus in alpine/snow-covered zones. Deficient in potash, phosphorus, and lime.
forest_mountain.distinctive_features: Heterogeneous profiles showing weak horizon differentiation; highly vulnerable to sheet and gully erosion on deforested slopes.
forest_mountain.major_crops: Tea, Coffee, Spices, Temperate Orchards (Apple, Pear, Peach, Walnut), Maize, Barley

alluvial.name: Alluvial Soils
alluvial.geological_origin: Depositional sediments laid down by the Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, and peninsular river deltas across the Indo-Gangetic trough.
alluvial.texture: Varies from sandy loam to silty loam and clayey; porous, soft, and easy to cultivate.
alluvial.chemical_profile: Rich in Potash and Phosphoric acid; moderately supplied with Lime. Markedly deficient in Nitrogen and Organic Humus.
alluvial.distinctive_features: Most agriculturally productive and widespread soil group (~40% of India's land area). Bhangar contains calcic nodules (Kankar), while Khadar is continuously renewed by annual floods.
alluvial.major_crops: Wheat, Rice, Sugarcane, Jute, Pulses, Oilseeds, Maize
states_covered: Coastal deltas of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu

red_yellow.name: Red and Yellow Soils
red_yellow.sub_type: Omnibus Group (Red in oxidized state, Yellow when hydrated)
red_yellow.geological_origin: Prolonged weathering of ancient crystalline igneous (granites, gneisses) and metamorphic rocks under low-rainfall conditions.
red_yellow.texture: Porous, crumbly, and friable structure; coarse-grained in uplands and fertile, finer-grained clayey in river valleys.
red_yellow.chemical_profile: Rich in Iron oxides (diffused iron imparting the distinct red hue) and Potash. Severely deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Humus, and Lime.
red_yellow.distinctive_features: Covers ~18% of India. Responds exceptionally well to chemical fertilizers and artificial irrigation.
red_yellow.major_crops: Groundnut, Millets (Ragi, Bajra), Tobacco, Pulses, Cotton, Oilseeds, Rice (in irrigated valley bottoms)

black.name: Black Soils (Regur)
black.geological_origin: In-situ weathering of Cretaceous volcanic basaltic lava sheets across the Deccan Traps.
black.texture: Extremely fine-grained and clayey (>50% clay content); highly plastic and sticky when wet.
black.chemical_profile: Rich in Lime, Iron, Magnesia, Alumina, Potash, and Calcium Carbonate. Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Organic Humus.
black.distinctive_features: Remarkable moisture-retention capacity; swells when wet and shrinks during summer dry periods, developing wide, deep cracks that cause natural aeration ('self-ploughing' effect).
black.major_crops: Cotton (classic Black Cotton soil), Soybean, Sugarcane, Jowar, Wheat, Sunflower, Tobacco

laterite.name: Laterite Soils
laterite.geological_origin: Intense tropical weathering under alternating heavy monsoon rainfall and dry heat; characterized by severe desilication and leaching.
laterite.texture: Coarse, porous, and vesicular structure; acidic (pH < 6.0); hardens permanently like rock when exposed to air (historically cut into building bricks).
laterite.chemical_profile: Rich in Iron Oxides and Aluminium; extremely poor in Silica, Nitrogen, Lime, Potash, Magnesia, and Humus (rapidly consumed by bacterial action under heat).
laterite.distinctive_features: Poor native fertility, but highly suited to intensive commercial plantation crops with systematic manuring.
laterite.major_crops: Cashew Nut, Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Coconut, Areca Nut, Cardamom
states_covered: Western Ghats crest (Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra)
Highlands of Odisha and Eastern Ghats

arid.name: Arid / Desert Soils
arid.geological_origin: Mechanical disintegration of parent rocks and extensive aeolian (wind-blown) dune deposition under arid climatic regimes.
arid.texture: Sandy to gravelly, loose, and highly permeable; virtually zero capillary retention.
arid.chemical_profile: High concentrations of soluble salts and Phosphates; extremely deficient in Nitrogen and Organic Humus. Lower soil horizons feature high Calcium carbonate (Kankar layers) that restrict water infiltration.
arid.distinctive_features: Can become remarkably productive with targeted canal irrigation (as demonstrated in the Ganganagar & Bikaner tracts along the Indira Gandhi Canal).
arid.major_crops: Drought-resistant crops: Bajra, Jowar, Guar, Pulses, Mustard, Barley, Cotton (irrigated)
